activity.lead: What happened on the machine: today, the history, alerts and live jobs.
activity.the_time_must_be_hh_mm: The time must be HH:MM (for example 22:00)
activity.if_you_stop_a_job_by: If you stop a job by hand and the End GCode never arrives, the next "start" closes it as "no end". It also works from any macro or the console.
activity.each_job_goes_into_the_history: ). Each job goes into the history with duration, zone/material, kWh and cost.
activity.a_live_job_streamed_line_by: A live job (streamed line by line over the network or USB, no file) is not a "job" for the machine and would not be logged. Paste these lines into the Start / End GCode of the program that sends it (in its device settings:
activity.which_events_to_notify_and_how: Which events to notify and how
activity.events_are_still_saved_in_the: Events are still saved in the history. It only affects the types marked "Hours" below; the emergency stop and fire ignore it unless you mark them.
activity.every_event_in_this_list_is: Every event in this list is saved in the history and, if its type is enabled below, it also arrives as a notification in the app
activity.filters_by_date_and_type_directly: Filters by date and type directly on the database (SQLite, "actividad" table) -- paginates the results instead of showing them all at once.
activity.attachment_hint: Photo or video from the chosen camera. The video ({s} s, recorded right after the event) arrives as a second, silent notification so the first one is not delayed. With no camera the notification is still sent without an attachment. Photos and videos of all notifications are turned off together on the Camera page (Settings: Camera photo in notifications).
activity.attachment_hint_no_camera: Photo or video from the chosen camera. The video ({s} s, recorded right after the event) arrives as a second, silent notification so the first one is not delayed. With no camera the notification is still sent without an attachment.
activity.no_details: This event has no saved details (it is older than this feature).
activity.tap_again_to_delete_this_event: Tap again to delete this event
activity.no_events_in_range_filter: No events in the chosen range/filter.
activity.delete_filtered_hint: Deletes ALL the events that match the current filter (dates, type and hide restarts), not just this page
activity.waiting_for_backend: Waiting for the backend (WorkshopService plugin / "System service")...
activity.android_ios_install_and_subscribe: (Android/iOS): install it and subscribe to the topic below.
activity.topic_keep_private: Topic (like a password: do not share it)
activity.new_topic_hint: Creates a new random topic; the phone stops receiving until you subscribe to the new one
activity.failures_n: {n} failures or stops in this list
activity.summary_no_jobs: No finished jobs in this range.
activity.summary_no_failures: No failures or stops: all in order.
activity.test_type_help: Sends a test notification of this type, with its attachment, priority and camera, even if the type is off or it is quiet hours.
activity.test_sent_photo: Test notification sent with a photo
activity.test_sent_video: Test notification sent; the video arrives a few seconds later
activity.only_mine_hint: Shows only the events done by you; the service filters them.
activity.help_summary_what: Counters of the chosen period built from the event history: jobs started, finished and cancelled, machine time, energy, errors, emergency stops and warnings. Service restarts are not counted.
activity.help_summary_why: To see in one look how the day (or the week) went, and which jobs and failures it had.
activity.help_summary_how: Choose Today, Yesterday or 7 days; Refresh reads it again.
activity.help_summary_jobs_what: One line per job in the period: start time, name, mode, duration and the energy it used. A cancelled job shows a different icon.
activity.help_summary_jobs_why: To check what ran and what each job cost in time and kWh.
activity.help_summary_failures_what: The errors, emergency stops and warnings the machine reported in the period, with their time. Emergency stops are red, the rest orange.
activity.help_summary_failures_why: To spot what went wrong without searching the whole history.
activity.help_history_what: The saved record of everything the machine did: jobs, faults, stops, alerts, changes. It is read from the service database in pages of 50.
activity.help_history_why: To find out what happened and when, and to export or clean it.
activity.help_history_how: Narrow it with the dates, the type, the text and the checkboxes, then press Find.
activity.help_range_what: The days the list is read from: a quick range (today, last days) or exact dates.
activity.help_range_why: The history can be long; the range keeps the search and the export to the days you need.
activity.help_kind_what: Only one kind of event: jobs, faults, emergency stops, alerts, changes and so on. The list shows the types that exist in the range.
activity.help_kind_why: To look at one thing without the noise of the rest.
activity.help_kind_how: Pick a type here or tap its coloured chip below; "All" removes the filter.
activity.help_hide_service_what: Leaves out the events that only say the Workshop service started or restarted.
activity.help_hide_service_why: Those lines appear every time the service reloads and bury the real events.
activity.help_hide_service_how: Untick it to see them, for example when you are chasing a restart problem.
activity.help_search_what: Looks for the text you type in the description, type and details of the events of the range. Press Enter or Find to apply it.
activity.help_search_why: To find a specific job, message or person quickly.
activity.help_group_what: Folds into one line the events that repeat: the same type and text, three or more in a row on the same day. The line shows how many and the time span.
activity.help_group_why: A fault that repeats hundreds of times would fill the page; grouped, it takes one line.
activity.help_group_how: Tap the grouped line to open the events inside it.
activity.help_mine_what: Narrows the history to the events done by the person who is signed in now.
activity.help_mine_why: To review your own actions without those of the rest of the team.
activity.help_export_what: Saves the events that match the current filter as a CSV file you can open in a spreadsheet. It reads them in blocks of 200, up to 5000 events.
activity.help_export_why: To keep a copy, send it or analyse it outside the panel.
activity.help_export_how: Set the range and filters first; the file contains the whole result, not only the page you see.
activity.help_table_what: One row per event: time, type (coloured chip), description, duration and energy. Chips show the mode and who did it.
activity.help_table_why: It is the detailed record behind the summary.
activity.help_table_how: Tap a row to open its details (data the machine sent). Delete is for technicians and needs two taps.
activity.help_delete_filtered_what: Deletes every event that matches the current filter (dates, type and hide restarts), not only the ones on this page.
activity.help_delete_filtered_why: To clean old or useless records.
activity.help_delete_filtered_how: Check the number on the button, then tap it twice. Only technicians see it.
activity.help_live_what: A job streamed line by line (network or USB, no file) is not a job for the machine, so it is not logged by itself. Two M118 lines in the Start and End GCode of the sending program mark its start and end.
activity.help_live_why: So live jobs also enter the history with duration, zone, material, kWh and cost.
activity.help_live_how: Copy the two lines into the Start GCode and End GCode of the program that sends the job.
activity.help_notices_what: Sends an alert to your phone through the ntfy app when an event you chose happens. The master switch turns all of them on or off.
activity.help_notices_why: To know about a fault or the end of a job without watching the screen.
activity.help_notices_how: Install ntfy, subscribe to the topic below, press Test, then choose the events.
activity.help_server_what: The ntfy server that delivers the alerts and the topic (the channel name) your phone subscribes to. Anyone who knows the topic can read the alerts.
activity.help_server_why: The service publishes to that topic and the phone receives from it.
activity.help_server_how: Use the public server unless you run your own. Keep the topic private, Save destination, then Test.
activity.help_new_topic_what: Creates a new random topic name and uses it from now on.
activity.help_new_topic_why: If someone else learned the old topic, they stop receiving your alerts.
activity.help_new_topic_missing: Your phone stops receiving alerts until you subscribe to the new topic.
activity.help_new_topic_how: Tap twice (the second tap confirms), then subscribe to the new topic in ntfy.
activity.help_quiet_what: A daily time window in which alerts are not sent, or are sent without sound. Events are still saved in the history.
activity.help_quiet_why: So the phone does not wake you at night for things that can wait.
activity.help_quiet_how: Set From and To, choose what happens during those hours, and turn the switch on. It only affects the event types that have "Hours" ticked.
activity.help_quiet_mode_what: What happens to an alert inside the quiet hours: "Do not send" drops it, "Send without sound" delivers it silently.
activity.help_quiet_mode_why: Lets you choose between total silence and a notification you read when you wake up.
activity.help_events_what: The list of event types the machine can report. Each has its own switch, a Test button and, once on, its attachment, priority and hours options.
activity.help_events_why: To get only the alerts you care about.
activity.help_events_how: Switch on the types you want. Test sends a sample of that type even if it is off or in quiet hours.
activity.help_video_what: Seconds of video recorded right after an event, for the types whose attachment is "Short video". It arrives as a second, silent notification.
activity.help_video_why: So the first alert is not delayed by the video.
activity.help_opt_attachment_what: Per event type: Attachment adds a photo or a short video from the camera; Priority sets how insistent the phone is (minimum has no sound, urgent is the loudest); Hours makes this type obey the quiet hours.
activity.help_opt_attachment_why: So an emergency stop can be loud with a photo while a minor warning stays silent.
activity.help_opt_attachment_how: The Hours box is only available when the quiet hours are on. The emergency stop and fire ignore the quiet hours unless it is ticked.

startup.title: Start-up
startup.state_na: does not apply to your machine
startup.make_tip: Copies the example to the SD card. It never overwrites a file that already exists.
startup.edit_tip: Opens the file in the DWC editor.
startup.hide_tip: Hides this row on this screen. It does not delete anything.
startup.service_tip: It has to be running: it makes the examples and answers the buttons of this plugin.
startup.service_sign_in: needs you to sign in to be checked
startup.service_role: your role cannot check it: a technician is needed
startup.locked: Not signed in: sign in to create or change files from here.
startup.row_history_tip: The service keeps the events of the machine here (jobs, modes, failures). It creates itself the first time.
startup.history_down: not answering: the database of the service does not reply
startup.row_alerts_tip: It is optional. With the alerts on and a topic, the service sends every important event to the phone through ntfy. It is set up in the Phone alerts section, or tap "Do not use".
startup.alerts_off: off (optional; switch them on in Phone alerts)
startup.alerts_no_topic: on but the server or the topic is missing
startup.assist_tip: Walks you through what is missing, one thing at a time. You can skip what you do not need.
startup.assist_no_action: This cannot be fixed with a file from here. Read the explanation and, when you have it, tap "Check again".
startup.assist_done_ready: Everything you went through is ready.
startup.assist_done_left: {n} left to do. You can start again whenever you like.
startup.create_help_tip: Asks a few questions and builds the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.questions_intro: Answer and I will build the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.err_range: The number is outside the allowed range.
startup.err_chars: Do not use quotes, semicolons or line breaks.
startup.err_pattern: It does not have the expected format. See the help of this field.
startup.warn_moves: {n} line(s) that move the machine were commented out with ";". Check them and remove the ";" only when you are sure and the machine is free.
startup.warn_active: Lines without ";" really run when you use the button.
startup.plan_example: {file} only has the example (all commented). It is replaced by this one, and the previous text is kept in {backup}.
startup.plan_new: {file} already has your configuration and I will not overwrite it. This one will be saved apart as {target}; when you have checked it, rename it in Files > Macros.
startup.verify_ok: Done: the file exists, has active instructions and the plugin already sees it.
startup.verify_new: Saved as {file}. The plugin keeps using the previous file until you swap the names.
startup.verify_comments: {file} was saved, but all its lines are still commented, so the plugin still takes it as an example. That may be what you wanted.
startup.verify_notseen: {file} was saved, but the plugin does not see it as ready yet. Tap "Check again" in a few seconds.
startup.verify_missing: I could not read {file} back. Tap "Check again" to verify it.
startup.verify_fail: It could not be saved ({error}). Nothing was changed.
startup.plan_changed: The file changed while you were answering. Check again what is going to happen and confirm once more.
startup.modal_hint: Tap a card to set it up, or let it walk you through step by step.
startup.modal_sub: Get ready what this plugin needs from your machine
startup.row_history_what: The database where the service writes down what happens on your machine: jobs, mode changes and faults.
startup.row_history_for: This page shows that list so you can see what happened and when.
startup.row_history_missing: The list stays empty. It is created by itself the first time the service writes something; if it does not appear, check that the service is running.
startup.row_alerts_what: Phone alerts through the ntfy app: every important event arrives as a notification.
startup.row_alerts_for: The service sends the alert when something important happens (a fault, the end of a job).
startup.row_alerts_missing: No alerts reach your phone; everything else works the same. It is optional: if you do not want them, tap "Do not use".
